item.title: Passkey campaign guidance separates platform nudges, attestation paths, and silent SSO — 12 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 12 October 2026

Passkey campaign guidance separates platform nudges, attestation paths, and silent SSO

The 12 October Entra ID updates focused on authentication guidance. The most consequential clarifications define how registration-campaign profiles are evaluated across platforms, where attested Authenticator passkeys can be registered, and when campaign nudges appear; examples also distinguish Windows Hello for Business from passkey profile restrictions.

Entra ID · Authentication

Campaign profiles have clearer platform-specific nudge rules

The guidance says unrestricted, synced-only, and device-bound-only profiles use platform-specific evaluation. AAGUID-restricted and attestation-enforced profiles suppress nudges across platforms after one eligible passkey is registered.

Entra ID · Authentication

Attested Authenticator passkeys follow different iOS and Android paths

iOS users can register attested passkeys only directly in the Authenticator app, while Android users can register them directly or through cross-device registration.

Entra ID · Authentication

Campaign prompts are tied to interactive MFA-satisfying sign-ins

Eligible users can see nudges during interactive sign-ins that satisfy MFA. Silent SSO events, including refresh token redemption, do not display registration-campaign nudges.

Entra ID · Authentication

Windows Hello for Business is evaluated separately from passkey profiles

The guidance states that Windows Hello for Business registration doesn’t follow passkey profile restrictions, so administrators should evaluate it separately when interpreting nudge suppression.

item.title: Key rotation reaches general availability while baseline enforcement guidance adds a Graph query — 9 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 9 October 2026

Key rotation reaches general availability while baseline enforcement guidance adds a Graph query

The strongest changes affect trust authentication, Conditional Access scoping, and Agent ID troubleshooting. Updated What's New guidance describes key rotation for incoming trust referral flows as generally available, improving reliability and addressing failures when referral tickets use a secondary key. Enforcement Resource Exclusions guidance records that baseline-scope enforcement rollout began June 15, 2026, and adds a Microsoft Graph query. New Agent ID how-to articles cover autonomous and interactive sign-ins, while a separate Kerberos trust guide details setup and lifecycle operations. The standalone Kerberos Server Key Rotation article was removed, and access-package guidance now clarifies a limitation on overlapping automatic-assignment policies.

Entra ID · Authentication

Generally available key rotation addresses secondary-key referral failures

The updated What's New guidance says key rotation for incoming trust referral flows is generally available. It describes the change as improving reliability and addressing authentication failures caused when referral tickets use a secondary key; no required administrator action is stated.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Baseline enforcement rollout gains a policy-discovery query

Enforcement Resource Exclusions guidance now states that baseline-scope enforcement rollout began June 15, 2026. It adds a Microsoft Graph query for finding affected Conditional Access policies and clarifies customization and sign-in review guidance.

Agent ID · Authentication

Autonomous Agent ID sign-ins get preview health-investigation guidance

A new how-to explains Health Monitoring signals and alerts, impact criteria, log correlation, troubleshooting, and prerequisites for autonomous agent sign-ins. The monitoring and alerts are documented as being in preview, with guidance for identifying affected applications and investigating application-only authentication failures.

Entra ID · Authentication

Kerberos trust guidance covers setup through trust removal

The new guide documents prerequisites, PowerShell module installation, Trusted Domain Object creation, client ticket configuration, key rotation, trust removal, and required permissions for managing trust between Microsoft Entra ID and on-premises AD DS.

ID Governance · Governance

Automatic assignment policies must not overlap for matched users

Entitlement Management guidance now clarifies that multiple automatic assignment policies for one access package are supported only when users do not match multiple policies simultaneously. Administrators should review overlapping policy scopes to avoid duplicate assignment paths.

View all updates for 9 October 2026 →

item.title: Entra outlines late-October passkey expansion for B2B and first MFA registration — 8 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 8 October 2026

Entra outlines late-October passkey expansion for B2B and first MFA registration

Two Microsoft Entra ID announcements point to a late-October 2026 authentication expansion. B2B users in resource tenants are slated to gain passkey registration and sign-in, while users generally will be able to register passkeys or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method without setting up SMS or voice first. Documentation updates also remove September rollout language, and Verified ID partner material adds HYPR.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

B2B users are slated to gain passkey registration and sign-in

Starting in late October 2026, resource tenants are expected to support passkey registration and sign-in for B2B users. Internal guest users will get Microsoft Authenticator app passkeys, while external users will not. The capability is described as enabled by default and intersecting with SMS and voice retirement policies.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Passkeys can become users’ first multifactor authentication method

A phased rollout beginning in late October 2026 will let users register passkeys or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method, removing the need to establish SMS or voice authentication first. The announcement says no user action is required.

Entra ID · Authentication

System-preferred authentication guidance removes September rollout wording

The article date changed to October 7, 2026, and the note describing gradual Microsoft-managed deployment through September 2026 was removed. The page no longer presents that September rollout language as ongoing.

Entra ID · Authentication

Registration campaign guidance drops its September completion estimate

The article no longer says the registration campaign rollout was expected to finish by the end of September 2026 or that tenant experiences might differ during the rollout. No administrator action is indicated in the supplied update.

Verified ID · General

HYPR is added to the Verified ID identity-verification partner gallery

The gallery now lists HYPR, links to its documentation, and describes its integration for workforce identity verification. Administrators and developers comparing partners can evaluate it for remote onboarding, secure access, and account recovery.

View all updates for 8 October 2026 →

item.title: Agent Conditional Access guidance now separates agent identities, user accounts, and OBO traffic — 7 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 7 October 2026

Agent Conditional Access guidance now separates agent identities, user accounts, and OBO traffic

Agent Conditional Access is the clear center of the 7 October update: a new Entra ID guide covers agents operating through their own user accounts, while Agent ID guidance separates agent identities, agent user accounts, and delegated or on-behalf-of access. The guidance directs administrators to match policy targeting to the token subject and check the stated licensing, role, device, network, registration, and OAuth prerequisites. A separate authentication update refreshes FIDO2 attestation data.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

New guide requires separate targeting for agent user accounts

The new Entra ID Conditional Access guide covers agent risk, compliant devices, and compliant networks for agents that use their own user accounts. It states that policies targeting all users do not include agent user accounts, so administrators must target agent users separately and satisfy the listed licensing, role, device, and network prerequisites.

Agent ID · Conditional Access

OBO guidance assigns Conditional Access targeting to the signed-in user

Updated Agent ID guidance says the signed-in user is the token subject for on-behalf-of traffic, whether targeted directly or through groups, and directs administrators to user-targeted policies for those resources. Selecting an agent identity is documented for a different access pattern.

Agent ID · Conditional Access

Autonomous-agent policy guidance adds prerequisites and report-only blocking

The revised guidance centers policies on agents using their own identities, adds licensing, role, registration, and OAuth prerequisites, and recommends report-only block policies for unapproved agents.

Entra ID · General

Policy guidance lists current licensing options and an upcoming Agent 365 requirement

The Policy Autonomous Agents page lists Microsoft 365 E7, or Microsoft Agent 365 paired with Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3, and says Agent 365 will soon be required.

Entra ID · Authentication

FIDO2 attestation reference moves to MDS 285 and adds five models

The attestation page now references MDS version 285 instead of 279 and adds five FIDO2 security-key models with their AAGUIDs and capability indicators. Administrators evaluating key attestation should use the updated identifiers.

View all updates for 7 October 2026 →

item.title: Cloud Sync supports hybrid-join device synchronization; Private Access 2.2.79 adds OTA updates — 6 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 6 October 2026

Cloud Sync supports hybrid-join device synchronization; Private Access 2.2.79 adds OTA updates

The most consequential updates clarify Cloud Sync support for Microsoft Entra hybrid join and document the Private Access Sensor 2.2.79 release, including its upgrade prerequisites. Entra administrators also get a more precise SSPR authentication-method count and stronger External ID passkey sample warnings. Most other changes were spelling, metadata, naming, or presentation edits.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Cloud Sync migration now includes hybrid-join device synchronization

The migration decision guide now states that Cloud Sync supports device synchronization for Microsoft Entra hybrid join. Device synchronization must be enabled separately, with updated migration guidance and configuration steps. Administrators moving hybrid-joined devices should include this capability explicitly in their migration plan.

Private Access · General

Private Access Sensor 2.2.79 adds OTA updates and Kerberos improvements

The release history records version 2.2.79, released September 29, 2026, with over-the-air sensor updates, enhanced Kerberos security and diagnostics, SID-based service matching, and corrected wildcard matching. Upgrading from version 2.2.42 requires a one-time full-installer deployment to enable OTA updates; inbound TCP and UDP port 1337 must be allowed, and IPv4 is required because IPv6 Kerberos traffic is blocked.

Entra ID · Authentication

SSPR counts Authenticator and OATH variants as one method

The SSPR guidance now states that Microsoft Authenticator, software OATH tokens, and hardware OATH tokens count as one authentication method, regardless of Authentication methods policy migration status. Administrators should use that shared count when evaluating SSPR method requirements.

External ID · Authentication

External ID passkey samples receive explicit high-privilege warnings

The updated guidance describes administrator-controlled passkey provisioning through the FIDO2 provisioning APIs and identifies the sample as testing-only. Its deletion flow uses high-privilege permissions and a client secret in browser code, so the sample should not be deployed in production.

External ID · Authentication

External-tenant SMS guidance distinguishes first-factor and SSPR use

The FAQ now states that SMS is unavailable for first-factor authentication in external tenants while indicating availability for self-service password reset. SMS remains available for second-factor verification at additional cost, giving administrators a clearer basis for external-tenant SSPR planning.

View all updates for 6 October 2026 →

item.title: App instance property-lock guidance broadens as External ID documents passkey API setup — 2 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 2 October 2026

App instance property-lock guidance broadens as External ID documents passkey API setup

Updated Entra ID guidance now describes app instance property locks for both single-tenant and multitenant applications, including the stated default for new applications since June 2026. A new Microsoft Entra External ID credential-management API reference covers signed-in customer passkey listing and registration, while Connect Health installation guidance identifies Global Administrator as the default account with agent-registration permission. Sponsors are also directed from My Access to My Account for guest management. Most remaining edits are narrower documentation corrections.

Entra ID · Security

App instance property-lock guidance covers single-tenant apps

The configuration article now says locks apply to an application's service principal for both single-tenant and multitenant applications. It also states that `Enable property lock` is enabled by default for new applications since June 2026 and points administrators to `servicePrincipalLockConfiguration`.

External ID · Authentication

External ID documents customer passkey credential-management API

The new reference explains how signed-in customers can list and register passkeys through the credential-management API, covering delegated authentication, permissions, and setup. Using the API requires manually provisioning its service principal and granting the appropriate delegated permission.

Entra ID · General

Connect Health agent-registration guidance names Global Administrator by default

The installation page now states that, by default, a Global Administrator account has permission to register the agent, replacing Hybrid Identity Administrator in the documented default.

ID Governance · Governance

Sponsored-guest instructions now point to My Account

The instructions now direct sponsors to `myaccount.microsoft.com` and the `Sponsored guests` item in the left navigation instead of My Access.

View all updates for 2 October 2026 →

item.title: SharePoint OTP retirement, Connect deadlines, and app-gallery onboarding reshape Entra administration — 1 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 1 October 2026

SharePoint OTP retirement, Connect deadlines, and app-gallery onboarding reshape Entra administration

SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication will retire across Microsoft 365 tenants starting in mid-October 2026, moving external sharing to Microsoft Entra B2B. Microsoft also opened self-service App Gallery onboarding in public preview ahead of general availability in mid-November, while Connect guidance separates a new AD FS/PingFederate hardening requirement from the broader Sync upgrade deadline.

External ID · Conditional Access

SharePoint OTP moves external sharing to Entra B2B in mid-October

SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication will retire starting in mid-October 2026 for all Microsoft 365 tenants. External users will need guest accounts under Microsoft Entra B2B, bringing SharePoint and OneDrive sharing under consistent governance and Conditional Access.

Entra ID · Standards

App Gallery opens self-service onboarding ahead of November GA

ISVs can now validate SSO and provisioning integrations, manage submissions, and track status in the Microsoft Entra admin center. The capability is in public preview, with general availability beginning in mid-November 2026.

Workload ID · Provisioning

AD FS and PingFederate hardening raises the Connect minimum

The documented requirement changes from Microsoft Entra Connect 2.5.79.0 to 2.6.84.0 or later. Application-based authentication is also required to maintain directory synchronization and avoid service disruptions.

Entra ID · Provisioning

General Connect Sync upgrade deadline moves to April 2027

The minimum-version deadline shifts from September 30, 2026, to April 7, 2027. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync 2.5.79.0 or later is required; synchronization services will fail until the upgrade is completed if the requirement is missed.

Workload ID · Authentication

SAP workload identities now require a matching API host

The updated guide removes its Preview label and states that workload identities are reusable only when their Application API host matches the provisioning app’s SAP SuccessFactors API host. It also adds the Application ID URI format and compatibility details for the September 15, 2026 update.

View all updates for 1 October 2026 →

Day in brief · 30 September 2026

item.title: New apps face COOP enforcement after January 31, 2027 — 24 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 24 September 2026

New apps face COOP enforcement after January 31, 2027

Microsoft Entra guidance sets a January 31, 2027 milestone for COOP policy enforcement on new applications, while Cloud Sync guidance expands coverage of provisioning Microsoft Entra users and groups into AD DS. The period also brings a concrete ChatWork SCIM retirement date and documents an Entra Connect hotfix for a Pass-through Authentication setup issue.

Entra ID · General

COOP policy gives new applications a January 31, 2027 compatibility deadline

New applications will be subject to Microsoft Entra COOP policy across web protocols after January 31, 2027. Popup-based sign-in may fail unless applications use a COOP-compatible flow such as MSAL.js v5. Applications that are not ready can temporarily opt out through the Microsoft Graph coopEnforcement property, then re-enable enforcement after migration.

Entra ID · Fundamentals

Cloud Sync guidance distinguishes preview user provisioning from generally available group provisioning

A new article documents groups-only, users-only, and users-and-groups provisioning from Microsoft Entra ID to AD DS. User provisioning is marked Preview, while group provisioning is generally available; the guidance also covers per-domain configuration limits and performance considerations.

Entra ID · Fundamentals

Cloud-managed users cannot use password writeback for password-based applications

Updated provisioning guidance states that password writeback is not supported for users created in Microsoft Entra ID. Password-based applications, including applications using LDAP binds, must be updated to Kerberos for cloud-managed users to use passwordless authentication.

Entra ID · Provisioning

ChatWork SCIM provisioning integration is scheduled for October 1 retirement

The ChatWork provisioning guide warns that SCIM-based provisioning will be discontinued on October 1, 2026, retiring the Microsoft Entra Enterprise App Gallery integration. Existing customers will no longer be able to provision users to ChatWork after that date.

Entra ID · General

Entra Connect 2.6.92 fixes a Pass-through Authentication setup failure

The version history identifies 2.6.92.0 as a fix for a 2.6.91.0 issue that could prevent Pass-through Authentication setup through the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard. Administrators on 2.6.79.0 are directed to uninstall it and install 2.6.92.0; those affected by the 2.6.91.0 issue can use the hotfix.

item.description:
Day in brief · 16 September 2026

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication face phased 2027 retirement deadlines

The strongest Entra guidance this period sets a February 1, 2027 retirement for Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication for users including internal guests, with Global Administrators and external users on July 1, 2027. Microsoft also added practical Cloud Sync migration and Connect Sync passwordless sign-in procedures, while most remaining activity involved Connect release-history, navigation, and command-path cleanup.

Entra ID · Authentication

Phased retirement guidance gives SMS and voice two deadlines

The authentication guidance states that Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire February 1, 2027, for users including internal guests. Global Administrators and external users follow July 1, 2027; after the applicable date, users whose only MFA method is SMS or voice receive a blocking passkey-registration prompt. Administrators should move them to phishing-resistant methods or configure a customer-managed telecom provider where needed.

Entra ID · General

Connect version guidance now identifies 2.6.91.0 as latest

The version history replaces references to 2.6.90.0 with 2.6.91.0 and identifies 2.6.91.0 as the latest available version. Upgrades involving an existing ADSync database should use 2.6.91.0 or later, while installations of recalled version 2.6.79.0 should be uninstalled and replaced with 2.6.91.0.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Cloud Sync migration guidance documents staged assessment and validation

A new article covers using the guided migration tool to assess an environment, create Cloud Sync configurations, run a preactivation check, and validate synchronization after migration. It also identifies required roles, credentials, eligibility limits, supported scenarios, and a two-week validation process.

Entra ID · Authentication

Connect Sync gets a documented FIDO2 and passkey sign-in path

Windows SSPR guidance moves from OMA-URI to Settings Catalog

item.description:

item.description:

Enterprise State Roaming shifts to Windows policies as Entra passkeys expand

The period’s strongest administrator change is the move of Enterprise State Roaming management out of the Entra admin center, alongside two scheduled passkey rollouts beginning in October 2026. item.description:
Day in brief · 3 September 2026

MCP server protection and a 98% managed-identity quota threshold anchor Entra guidance

The strongest changes are new implementation guidance for securing Model Context Protocol servers with Microsoft Entra ID and integrating Entitlement Management with ServiceNow. The passkey page now omits “(preview)” from its title and heading, with the supplied evidence indicating a label change.

Entra ID · Standards

New MCP server protection procedure uses Entra OAuth and Agent ID

A new Entra ID how-to explains registering an MCP server as an OAuth 2.0 protected resource, enabling v2 access tokens, and connecting MCP clients through Microsoft Entra Agent ID. An app registration with required permissions and an HTTPS MCP server are prerequisites.

Entra ID · Governance

Entitlement Management documents ServiceNow access-package workflows

New guidance covers ServiceNow access package requests, request history, and approvals, along with installation, configuration, licensing, and user workflows. Microsoft Entra ID Entitlement Management remains the system of record, and a Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra Suite license is required.

Workload ID · General

Managed identity creation is blocked at 98% directory quota usage

The updated guidance states that creating a managed identity is blocked when directory usage reaches or exceeds 98% of the tenant quota, including for new or recreated service principals. Existing identities and assignments continue to work; soft-deleted objects count toward the quota, and reducing usage or increasing the quota enables retries.

PIM audit tracing now pivots on roleAssignmentRequestId

Related PIM activation and deactivation events can have different CorrelationId values. The updated audit-log guidance recommends roleAssignmentRequestId for tracing a complete request and adds Log Analytics query examples.

Entra ID · Developer

App Gallery publishing guidance now requires the Partner One ID

The publishing prerequisites now instruct app publishers to provide a Partner One ID associated with the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program organization listed as the publisher, and explain where to get help if the identifier is unknown.

item.description:

Cloud Sync group provisioning guidance shifts to focused AD DS workflows and constraints

The period is dominated by a substantial restructuring of Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync guidance for provisioning groups to Active Directory. Microsoft added a dedicated AD DS tutorial, rewrote setup and testing material, documented tighter topology requirements, and removed seven older pages covering combined provisioning, prerequisites, deployment options, and test-and-enable procedures. Cloud Sync adds a dedicated group-provisioning tutorial for AD DS

Conditional Access guidance documents Android Play Integrity enforcement

The Assignment Network guidance now says Microsoft Authenticator for Android uses the Google Play Integrity API for jailbreak detection and denies access when the API is unavailable, unless the policy is disabled. Use this detail when troubleshooting blocked Android access under Conditional Access.

item.description:

First-factor system-preferred authentication rolls out as Lifecycle Workflow guidance expands to 365 days

Microsoft Entra is applying system-preferred authentication to first-factor sign-ins for tenants in the Microsoft-managed state, with rollout continuing through late September 2026. ID Governance guidance now documents 365-day event offsets and clarifies the Time based attribute V2 trigger, while Global Secure Access records an August macOS client release with new controls and deployment considerations. Entra ID · Authentication

System-preferred authentication now covers first-factor sign-ins

For tenants in the Microsoft-managed state, Microsoft Entra now selects the most secure registered authentication method for first-factor sign-ins. Rollout runs from late June through late September 2026; administrators can keep or change the setting and should update user guidance.

ID Governance · Governance

Lifecycle Workflow guidance documents 365-day event offsets

The updated Execution Conditions page now states that the limits for Days from event, and Days to event when using Between, increased from 180 to 365 days. It describes conditions up to one year before or after an event and states that no administrator action is required.

ID Governance · Fundamentals

The documentation describes Exactly, Less than or equal to, and Between comparisons with offsets from 0 to 180 days before or after supported date attributes. Release notes for August 21, 2026 list Home Network traffic controls, a Connections page, agentic detection support, and Secure DNS bypass, along with connectivity, sign-in, tunnel, cache-reset, and crash fixes. Administrators should review the release when planning macOS deployments.

Global Secure Access · General

The installation page states that client version 1.1.26060207 includes com.microsoft.autoupdate2 and that an existing installation may conflict with Intune detection rules. It advises optionally removing that app from the Included apps list.

ID Governance task guidance now applies “Remove all access package assignments for user” to both leaver and mover templates. For mover templates, scheduled removal defaults to 15 days; administrators can customize the timing or choose immediate removal.

item.title: Federated sign-in validation tightens as Windows Hello and macOS SSO gain standalone MFA — 18 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 18 August 2026

Federated sign-in validation tightens as Windows Hello and macOS SSO gain standalone MFA

The day’s consequential changes are two Entra authentication behavior updates. Microsoft says the federatedTokenValidationPolicy default will block federated sign-ins when internalDomainFederation does not match the user’s UPN domain for federated domains configured before December 2025. Starting in October 2026, Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO will count as standalone MFA factors. Workload ID’s flexible federated identity credential preview guidance also tightens GitHub claim matching, while the remaining updates are lower-impact synchronization and licensing reference maintenance.

External ID · Conditional Access

FederatedTokenValidationPolicy default will block mismatched federated domains

Microsoft’s Message Center notice describes a mid-August 2026 default change affecting federated domains configured before December 2025. Federated sign-ins will be blocked when internalDomainFederation does not match the user’s UPN domain. Administrators can customize the policy through Microsoft Graph, although Microsoft discourages customization.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Windows Hello and macOS Platform SSO become standalone MFA factors

Starting in October 2026, Microsoft Entra will recognize Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors, allowing users to satisfy MFA requirements without an additional passkey. Microsoft says no configuration changes are required, but onboarding and MFA-registration guidance should be updated.

Workload ID · Security

GitHub flexible FIC preview guidance requires immutable repository claims

The updated preview documentation says GitHub flexible federated identity credentials must match sub and at least one immutable claim: repository_id or repository_owner_id. The examples and operator guidance now use these claims with the eq operator when defining or reviewing trust.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Synchronization guidance adds sAMAccountName coverage for Domain Services

The Synchronization page now describes enhanced support for synchronizing sAMAccountName with Microsoft Entra Domain Services and links to dedicated guidance for that scenario.

Entra ID · General

Licensing reference adds Windows 10 ESU identifiers to Windows 365 entries

The reference, updated August 14, 2026, adds Windows 10 ESU service-plan identifiers to two Windows 365 plan entries. No administrator action is stated beyond using the updated reference when matching those plans.

item.title: Agent ID guidance now directs provisioning through identity blueprints, not app registrations — 14 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 14 August 2026

Agent ID guidance now directs provisioning through identity blueprints, not app registrations

14 August produced no new or removed entries and was dominated by documentation maintenance, particularly across Microsoft Entra Agent ID. The most consequential update clarifies that agents should use identity blueprints and the #Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity object rather than standard application-registration APIs. Other notable edits clarify Identity Protection remediation, dynamic-group treatment of agent accounts, replica-set networking, and a Windows passkey preview label; none of the supplied diffs independently announces a new feature or general availability.

Agent ID · Architecture

Agent ID provisioning guidance moves to identity blueprints

The architecture guidance now directs administrators to create agents from an agent identity blueprint and the #Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity object, rather than through standard application-registration APIs. It also documents supported creation channels, roles, permissions, and .NET usage. This is a guidance clarification, not a separately announced launch.

ID Protection · Authentication

Identity Protection clarifies the attacker-added-device response

The Identity Protection Policies article replaces “Device disablement” with “Attacker-added device” and spells out the documented response: the Entra device object is disabled, new token issuance is blocked, device-bound refresh tokens are revoked, and user sessions are revoked. The supplied change clarifies the remediation scope rather than announcing a new control.

Entra ID · General

Dynamic-group guidance now covers agent user accounts

Microsoft Entra ID guidance now explains that agent user accounts are evaluated by user-based membership rules and are not distinguished from other users by default. Administrators can explicitly include or exclude them, including accounts associated with a particular agent identity blueprint.

Entra ID · Fundamentals

Replica-set guidance makes full virtual-network meshing explicit

The replica-set documentation now states that all virtual networks hosting replica sets must be connected. It also specifies that replica sets are deployed in one Active Directory site and depend on a fully meshed virtual-network topology, clarifying a deployment prerequisite.

Entra ID · Authentication

Windows passkey registration loses its preview label

The “Register a Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows” page no longer includes “(preview)” in its title or heading. No procedural change is shown, and the supplied diff does not explicitly announce general availability or a product launch.

item.title: Entra ID Free SMS first-factor sign-in retirement makes alternate authentication necessary — 13 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 13 August 2026

Entra ID Free SMS first-factor sign-in retirement makes alternate authentication necessary

The period’s main administrator-impacting notice is Microsoft’s planned retirement of SMS first-factor sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants on 11 August 2026 because of fraud risks; SMS used for multifactor authentication remains unaffected. Microsoft also added first-party Workload ID federation tutorials for Google Cloud and SPIFFE/SPIRE, expanded Agent ID permission guidance, and revised Catalog Access Reviews documentation. Most remaining edits were maintenance, including a corrected Global Secure Access section name and updated links.

Entra ID · Authentication

SMS first-factor sign-in retirement for Entra ID Free tenants

A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says Microsoft will retire SMS first-factor sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants on 11 August 2026 because of fraud risks. Users must switch to another authentication method before retirement; SMS as a multifactor method is unaffected. This is a security-related product retirement, not a documentation clarification.

ID Governance · Governance

Catalog Access Reviews documentation adds a 12-hour data-freshness caveat

Updated ID Governance guidance removes Preview labels, broadens reviewer terminology beyond managers, and warns that changes made within 12 hours before a review starts may not appear. The supplied evidence does not explicitly announce general availability, so the status change should not be treated as a confirmed GA announcement.

Workload ID · General

Google Cloud workload federation gets a first-party Workload ID tutorial

A new tutorial shows how an Entra application can trust a Google-issued service-account token, exchange it for an Entra access token, and access Azure resources without storing application secrets. It documents a configuration scenario rather than announcing a new product launch and requires permission to add a federated identity credential.

Workload ID · General

SPIFFE/SPIRE workload federation gets a first-party Workload ID tutorial

A new tutorial documents exchanging a Kubernetes workload’s SPIFFE JWT-SVID for a Microsoft Entra access token so it can access Azure resources without stored secrets. The page is implementation guidance for an existing federation scenario, not evidence of a new product launch.

Agent ID · Developer

Agent ID guidance maps Microsoft 365 channels to required permissions

Updated guidance now covers agents communicating through Outlook email, OneDrive and SharePoint comments, Teams chats, and Teams channels, with permissions for receiving events and sending responses. Administrators can use the channel-by-channel table to configure agent access; no underlying product behavior change is stated.
